title: Completion reflects cokernel torsion on a fixed closed thickening
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $I,K$ be quasi-coherent ideal sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme], and let $q,s\geq1$. Assume for every Noetherian instance on $Z=V(K^q)$ that completion of coherent modules on $Z$ with respect to $I\mathcal O_Z$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal, def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] is an equivalence. Let $F,G$ be coherent modules and $a:F\to G$ a morphism, with $K^qF=K^qG=0$. If for every $n\geq0$ the ordinary cokernel of $F/I^{n+1}F\to G/I^{n+1}G$ is annihilated by $K^s$, then the ordinary cokernel of $a$ is annihilated by $K^{2s}$. All cokernels and ideal products are in the ambient category of sheaf modules.

source.place: Tag 088A (lemma-existence-tricky), second use of Remark 0888; Tag 087T identifies coherent modules on a closed thickening; proof expanded using right exactness for the cokernel alone

proof.text: Put Q = cokernel(a) and B = K^s Q with inclusion j. Coherent cokernel closure makes Q coherent. Reuse the proved private idealSheafPower_quasicoherent and idealModuleProduct_quasicoherent lemmas of CoherentFormalModule to obtain quasi-coherence of B; the coherent submodule clause makes B coherent. Reuse idealModuleProduct_quotient_comp_zero_iff to pass K^q annihilation from G to Q, and idealModuleProduct_zero_of_mono to pass it to B. These existing lemmas use right exactness of tensor products and naturality of multiplication.

Set i:Z=V(K^q)→X. The power quotient comparison identifies each quotient by K^q with pushforward of tensor pullback, preserving the quotient projection as the adjunction unit. Annihilation makes that projection invertible. The unit-kernel comparison then gives support of Q and B on Z. Completion on Z followed by inclusion and termwise closed pushforward is faithful. The coherent closed-immersion equivalence, the natural completion comparison, and essential surjectivity of the equivalence transport this faithfulness to the completion functor on supported coherent modules of X.

For every positive level, reduction of the epimorphism G→Q is epimorphic: its composite with the source quotient projection is the composite of G→Q with the target quotient projection. It kills the reduction of a, so factors through the reduced cokernel by cokernel.desc. This factor is epi by cancellation. Passing the given K^s annihilation through this epimorphism kills the ideal product of Q/I^(n+1)Q. formalModuleQuotient_factor applied to Q→Q/I^(n+1)Q gives j followed by that projection equal to zero. Cancel the source quotient projection in the definition of formalModuleQuotientMap to show that each component of the completion of j is zero.

View j and the zero map between supported coherent objects. Their completions agree componentwise, so the faithful functor of step 2 identifies them. Thus j=0; because j is mono, B is zero. Factor the inclusion K^(2s)Q through K^s Q using formalModuleQuotient_factor at the identity of Q and s≤2s. The lower inclusion is zero, hence the higher inclusion is zero and its monic source is zero.

lean.statement:
theorem completion_thickening_cokernel_reflection
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I K : X.IdealSheafData)
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q)
    (hcomplete : ∀ hZ : IsNoetherian (K ^ q).subscheme,
      Functor.IsEquivalence
        (@completion ((K ^ q).subscheme) hZ (I.comap (K ^ q).subschemeι)))
    (F G : CoherentModules X) (a : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι q).2
      F.obj))
    (hG : IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι q).2
      G.obj))
    (s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s)
    (hred : ∀ n : ℕ,
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι s).2
        (cokernel (formalModuleQuotientMap I a.hom (Nat.le_refl (n + 1)))))) :
    IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι (2 * s)).2
      (cokernel a.hom))
